submissions.title: Lambda to build new data center in Lowndes County, Alabama, investing more than $33 billion in state
submissions.excerpt: investing more than $33 billion in state
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT, well above the $1B/100MW threshold. Four-building 'Project Red Clay' campus (~800 acres) developed with Cloverleaf Infrastructure; secondary reporting (AL Reporter, Baxtel) puts the figure precisely at $33.1 billion, creating 1,000+ construction jobs and 225+ permanent jobs, with closed-loop cooling; electricity supply still subject to regulatory approval, construction timeline up to 5 years. No confirmed MW figure found anywhere -- leave power blank, do not guess. Local opposition active: a residents' group and the Alabama Rivers Alliance sued Lowndes County commissioners over a tax abatement tied to the deal approved 3-2 on 2026-10-13; sources disagree sharply on the abatement's size ($1.1B vs $2.7B reported by different outlets) so flag that figure as unresolved rather than use either number. submissions.title: Boise City Council approves 6-month moratorium on large data center construction
submissions.excerpt: facilities larger than 100,000 square feet or those with a projected power demand of at least 20 megawatts
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Boise, ID city council voted unanimously on 2026-11-10 for an immediate 6-month emergency moratorium on new large-data-center applications, triggered by any facility >=100,000 sq ft OR >=20MW projected demand at full buildout. Projects with planning approval already granted are grandfathered and unaffected. The city states no mega-data-center applications are currently pending inside city limits; Idaho Capital Sun separately flags a proposed ~4-million-sq-ft project just south of the city (outside this ordinance's jurisdiction) as the likely real target -- worth a human follow-up to see if that project is one we track. This agent cross-checked the 103-project local tracker snapshot and found no currently-tracked BEP project sited in Boise city limits, so no projectId is attached. Article-sourced (news coverage of the council vote), not the ordinance text itself -- a human reviewer may want to pull the actual Boise ordinance number for a primary cite.

submissions.title: Voters back data center limits in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states
submissions.excerpt: Voters back data center limits in 40 of 41 ballot measures across 10 states
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION, broad/national signal rather than one project: the 2026-11-03 US midterm ballot produced the largest coordinated wave yet of local data-center restrictions -- roughly 40 of 41 measures passed across 10 states per Baxtel/Ballotpedia (a Venable LLP client alert dated 2026-11-04 corroborates with a count of 41 measures in 10 states; the Washington Post's narrower count was >=38 jurisdictions, so treat the exact tally as approximate across outlets). Ohio accounted for 21 of the measures, including charter amendments in Piqua and Upper Sandusky that flatly prohibit data center construction; Wiscasset, ME adopted a 6-month moratorium. The lone reported rejection was in Harwood, ND. This agent did not find a currently-tracked BEP project located in any of the named jurisdictions (cross-checked against the 103-project local snapshot), but a human reviewer should double check the Ohio and Maine sites specifically since this agent could not exhaustively verify every affected locality against the tracker's location fields.
